title: Ways of learning: supervised, unsupervised, self-supervised

sections.skill: Tell supervised, unsupervised and self-supervised learning apart

questions.prompt: Photos are each labeled "cat" or "dog" for training. Which kind of learning is this?

choices.text: Unsupervised, because the model sorts photos by itself
Supervised
Self-supervised, because photos contain their own answers
No learning, because photos cannot teach a model anything

questions.intro: Models learn from different kinds of SIGNALS. In SUPERVISED learning, each training example comes with a label, the right answer: photos marked "cat" or "dog," emails marked "spam" or "not spam." In UNSUPERVISED learning, there are no labels; the model looks for structure on its own, such as grouping customers with similar shopping habits. In SELF-SUPERVISED learning, the data supplies its own answers: hide a word in a sentence and train the model to predict it. Large language models are mostly trained this way, because huge amounts of text need no hand-made labels.
questions.feedback: Labeled examples mean supervised learning.

sections.skill: Compare three ways a student might learn

questions.prompt: The student with the answer key is like which kind?

choices.text: Unsupervised learning, since she sorts things alone
Supervised learning
Self-supervised learning, since the novel checks her
No learning at all, since answer keys are cheating

questions.intro: Picture three students. The first works through a WORKBOOK with an answer key: she checks each answer and learns from corrections (like supervised learning). The second gets a box of mixed seashells with no instructions and sorts them into piles that look alike (like unsupervised learning). The third covers one word in each sentence of a novel and guesses it, then uncovers it to check (like self-supervised learning). All three learn, but from different kinds of signals.
questions.feedback: Checking against given answers is supervised.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Combine learning stages and question "taught itself" claims

questions.prompt: A model learned from web text, then from labeled examples, then from human ratings. Which is accurate?

choices.text: It used only unsupervised learning from start to finish
It combined several kinds of learning
It used only rules written by programmers
It used no training data at any stage

questions.correct_answer: It combined several kinds of learning
questions.intro: Real systems often combine these. A language model might first learn by self-supervision on huge amounts of text, then be adjusted with a smaller set of labeled, human-written examples (supervised), then with human ratings. Each stage has its own risks: unlabeled text carries whatever patterns and biases the text contains, labels can be wrong, and groupings found without labels may not mean what people assume. When someone says a model "taught itself," ask what signal it actually learned from.
questions.feedback: Real systems often combine stages.
